h: Why It Is Called Sinai: Miracles of the Soul and a Good Sign

p: That miracles were performed on it?
"That a good sign was made on it?
Then it should be called 'Har Simanai.'"
This implies that were it not for the difficulty
the explanation would have been fine.
Now this needs to be understood:
what miracles were performed on it for Yisrael?
that a good sign was made —
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
according to what is written in the holy Zohar
all the miracles..." and so on,
until: "and they reach the zayin..." and so on,
"then He performs miracles..." and so on.
when there is a revelation of Atika
reaching down to the attribute of Malchus.
"for the miracles and for the wonders";
and the words of Your wonders I will speak...;
and Your greatness I will recount" (Tehillim 145:3-6).
up to the level of Atika, Ein Sof:
"And the words of Your wonders I will speak."
Now miracles of the body occur constantly,
and the beneficiary of a miracle
in the forty-nine gates of impurity,
like a fetus in its mother's womb, as is known,
and Hashem Yisbarach took them out.
Now on the first night of Pesach
there was a revelation of Atika
in the tenth plague, the Plague of the Firstborn,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב כט, א):
the Holy One, blessed be He, began";
in the manner written in the holy Zohar
עַד אַחַר כָּךְ בִּקְרִיעַת יַם סוּף,
until afterward, at the Splitting of the Sea,
where "a maidservant saw at the sea..." and so on
on "And they went out into the wilderness of Shur":
"What is 'the wilderness of Shur'..." and so on,
"for they wished to gaze..." and so on.
But the essential revelation of Atika
as it says in the holy Zohar
what Yechezkel did not see..." and so on.
And this is the "miracles performed on it" for Yisrael:
אֲנִי אָמַרְתִּי אֱלֹהִים אַתֶּם (תְּהִלִּים פב, ו).
And on this the Gemara asks:
"that a good sign was made on it," and so on.
the yetzer hara returned to its place,
it is no longer fitting to call it
"I am" and "You shall have no other gods" —
by which the learning of Torah was implanted in their hearts
and the yetzer hara uprooted from their hearts,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה א, ב),
so that each one can afterward
יִתָּכֵן עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת סז, א):
may be explained by what Chazal say (Shabbos 67a):
but because you are low..." and so on;
And this is the good sign:
"just as water leaves a high place".
and it was said of them:
that then, at the time of Matan Torah,
so that they would not have died,
and the Angel of Death was nullified —
It was effective as a good sign:
that even though the defect of the serpent returned,
"'When you lie down, it shall guard over you' — this is death;
'and when you awaken, it shall converse with you' —

inlineHeadings.text: What miracles were done at Har Sinai?
A miracle: the revelation of Atika
The miracle of Yetzias Mitzrayim in the soul
The essential revelation at Matan Torah
A good sign: low like the thornbush
Even after they sinned: death as sleep

paragraphs.text: Shabbos 89a — "One of the Rabbis asked Rav Kahana: Have you heard what 'Mount Sinai' means? He said: A mountain on which miracles (nisim) were done for Israel. — Then it should be called Mount Nisai! — Rather, a mountain on which a good sign (siman) was made for Israel. — Then it should be called Mount Simanai!… Rav Chisda and Rabbah son of Rav Huna said: It is the mountain from which hatred (sinah) descended upon the idolaters."

paragraphs.text: Zohar II 54a (Beshalach) — "Rather, thus we learned: all the miracles and all the mighty deeds that were done for Israel — when the light of the Holy Atika shines in its crowns, engraved and inscribed… then it performs miracles and mighty deeds."

paragraphs.text: Niddah 31a — "This is what Rabbi Elazar said: What is meant by 'Who does great wonders alone' (Tehillim 72:18)? Even the beneficiary of a miracle does not recognize his miracle."

rich.text: — "This is what Rabbi Elazar said: What is meant by 'Who does great wonders alone' (Tehillim 72:18)? Even the beneficiary of a miracle does not recognize his miracle."

paragraphs.text: Zohar II 29a (Vaera) — "Come and see: He struck first at the lowest of all the levels. Rabbi Shimon said: The Holy One began from below, and His hand struck with each and every finger; and when it reached the highest level of all, He did His own deed — He passed through the land of Egypt and slew all; therefore He slew all the firstborn in Egypt, for it is the highest level, the firstborn of all."

paragraphs.text: Zohar II 36a (Bo) — "'And Hashem will strike Egypt, striking and healing' (Yeshayahu 19:22): striking for Egypt and healing for Israel. What healing? Since they were circumcised, they needed healing."

paragraphs.text: Zohar II (Beshalach) — "They would not journey until Moshe took hold of them and showed them the radiance of the glory of the Holy One in the wilderness; from their great longing and desire to gaze at it, Moshe led them away… 'And they went out to the wilderness of Shur' (Shemos 15:22) — what is the wilderness of Shur? The wilderness where they longed to gaze."

paragraphs.text: Shabbos 67a — "And let him say thus: O bush, O bush — not because you are taller than all trees did the Holy One rest His Shechinah upon you, but because you are lower than all trees did the Holy One rest His Shechinah upon you."

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Pesach 25 — “The completion of the fruit is on Shavuos, the time of Matan Torah, of which it is written, ‘I said: You are G-dly beings,’ for they would not have died (Avodah Zarah 5a); and this is that they merited then the upper Shabbos, and the evil inclination departed from there (Tikkunei Zohar 48)… but after the corruption, ‘you have corrupted your deeds’…” Connection: The same verses, “I said: You are G-dly beings… you have corrupted your deeds,” read of Matan Torah and its loss.

paragraphs.text: Sotah 21a — “‘When you lie down it shall guard you’—this is death; ‘and when you awake it shall speak with you’—in the World to Come.”
